title: Fibrewise criterion for a nonzero finitely presented module stalk
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] with morphisms $p:X\to S$, $q:Y\to S$, $f:X\to Y$ satisfying $q\circ f=p$. Suppose $p$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], $q$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Fix $x\in X$, set $y=f(x)$ and $s=p(x)$, and assume $\mathcal F_x\ne0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let $i_s:X_s\to X$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre projection and $f_s:X_s\to Y_s$ the induced morphism [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product]. Denote by $\widetilde x\in X_s$ the point mapping to $x$, and put $\mathcal F_s=i_s^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $\mathcal F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and $(\mathcal F_s)_{\widetilde x}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{Y_s,f_s(\widetilde x)}$, then $\mathcal F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $q$ is flat at $y$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Module flatness means that tensoring with the module preserves exact sequences; all scalar actions are induced by the displayed scheme morphisms. No flatness of $p$ and no Noetherian hypothesis are assumed.

source.place: Tag 039C, theorem-criterion-flatness-fibre, implication (1) to (2), without the openness clause.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $C=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $M=\mathcal F_x$. The compatible-stalk-data lemma gives a tower of nonzero local rings $R\to B\to C$, with composite the stalk map of $p$, with $C$ essentially finitely presented over $R$ and $B$ essentially of finite type over $R$. It also identifies the fibre local rings with $C/\mathfrak m_RC$ and $B/\mathfrak m_RB$, and their map with the quotient of $B\to C$. Choose a finite local presentation of $\mathcal F$ at $x$, which exists by the finite-presentation hypothesis; the finite-presentation stalk lemma makes $M$ finitely presented over $C$. In particular it is finite over $C$. It is nonzero and $R$-flat by hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 039C, theorem-criterion-flatness-fibre, first paragraph of proof; modules Tag 01CP, finite local presentations on stalks.

proof.text: The pullback-stalk formula for $i_s$ identifies $(\mathcal F_s)_{\widetilde x}$ with $M\otimes_C\mathcal O_{X_s,\widetilde x}$. Using the quotient isomorphism of step 1 and the quotient-tensor lemma, this is $M/\mathfrak m_RM$: explicitly $m\otimes[c]\mapsto[cm]$, with inverse $[m]\mapsto m\otimes1$. The submodule $(\mathfrak m_RC)M$ equals $\mathfrak m_RM$ because both consist of finite sums of products of images of elements of $\mathfrak m_R$ with elements of $M$. The $B/\mathfrak m_RB$-action is $[b][m]=[\beta(b)m]$, by the compatible fibre stalk maps in step 1. Thus the given fibre flatness says precisely that $M/\mathfrak m_RM$ is flat over $B/\mathfrak m_RB$.

source.place: Tag 039C, theorem-criterion-flatness-fibre, first paragraph of proof; sheaves Tag 0098, lemma-stalk-pullback-modules; algebra Tag 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact, applied to the quotient presentation.

proof.text: Apply the finite-type local closed-fibre approximation to $R\to B$. It supplies a nonzero local, essentially finitely presented $R$-algebra $T$ and a surjective local $R$-algebra map $u:T\to B$, with $T/\mathfrak m_RT\cong B/\mathfrak m_RB$ via $[t]\mapsto[u(t)]$. Give $C$ and $M$ their $T$-actions through $B$. The composite $T\to B\to C$ is local. Across the displayed isomorphism, the action on $M/\mathfrak m_RM$ is $[t][m]=[\beta(u(t))m]$, so its flatness in step 2 is flatness over $T/\mathfrak m_RT$ as well. Apply the existing fibre criterion to $R\to T\to C$ and the $C$-module $M$. Both required algebras $T,C$ are essentially finitely presented over $R$; $M$ is finitely presented over $C$, nonzero, $R$-flat, and its closed fibre is flat over $T/\mathfrak m_RT$. The criterion gives $T$ flat over $R$ and $M$ flat over $T$.

source.place: Tag 05UV, lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-fp-over-ft, finite-presentation approximation and application of Tag 00R7, lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre.

proof.text: Since $T\to C$ is local, $\mathfrak m_TM\subseteq\mathfrak m_CM$. If $\mathfrak m_TM=M$, then $\mathfrak m_CM=M$; Nakayama over the local ring $C$, applied to the finite $C$-module $M$, would give $M=0$, a contradiction. Therefore $M/\mathfrak m_TM\ne0$. The nonzero-closed-fibre criterion for a flat module now makes the $T$-flat module $M$ faithfully flat over $T$. Notice that finiteness is needed over $C$, not over $T$.

source.place: Tag 00DV, lemma-NAK, part (4), with zero submodule; Tag 00HP, lemma-ff, (4) implies (1).

proof.text: Let $K=\ker(u)$. It annihilates $M$, since the $T$-action factors through $B$. Tensor the inclusion $K\hookrightarrow T$ with $M$. Flatness makes $K\otimes_TM\to T\otimes_TM\cong M$ injective, and this map sends $k\otimes m$ to $km=0$. Hence $K\otimes_TM=0$. Faithful flatness reflects exactness of the complex $0\to K\to0$, so $K=0$. Thus the surjective map $u$ is an isomorphism. Under $T\cong B$, the two scalar actions agree: $u(t)m=tm$ and the map $R\to B$ is $u$ composed with $R\to T$. Consequently the tensor functors testing $R$-flatness of $B$ and $B$-flatness of $M$ are isomorphic to those testing $R$-flatness of $T$ and $T$-flatness of $M$; the isomorphisms send pure tensors to the same tensors with $u$ or $u^{-1}$ on the ring factor. Step 3 therefore proves both required flatness assertions. The first says exactly that $q$ is flat at $y$.
